signup_bonus_continuity.name: Continuity Bonus Offer
signup_bonus_continuity.summary: Offer a high-value bonus (worth MORE than the first payment) when customers sign up for continuity TODAY. Creates urgency and increases immediate conversion.

target_metrics.bonus_hunter_churn: Monitor—should be minimal if bonus is aligned

signup_bonus_continuity.hormozi_principle: The bonus must have more perceived value than the first continuity payment. This flips the psychology—they're getting MORE value than they're paying for month one.

tasks.description: Select something with high perceived value but low marginal cost to you

tasks.task: Calculate bonus value vs. first payment
tasks.description: Ensure the math makes the offer irresistible
tasks.example: Monthly: $59/mo, Bonus: $800 value of past products → They get $800 for $59

tasks.task: Ensure bonus relates to core offer
tasks.description: Bonus should attract people who want your main thing
tasks.principle: Related bonuses attract right customers; unrelated bonuses attract bonus hunters who churn

tasks.description: Instant gratification reinforces their decision
Explain what they get every month
tasks.format: Every month you get [X, Y, Z] for just $X/month

tasks.description: Show all bonus components with crossed-out prices
Bonus only available for immediate signup
tasks.script: 'This bonus is only available if you join TODAY. After this call, it's gone.'
tasks.enforcement: Actually remove the bonus after the window

tasks.description: Show how bonus + ongoing subscription = complete solution
tasks.example: 'The bonus gives you everything we've ever created. The membership gives you everything we'll create going forward.'

tasks.description: If churn spikes after bonus campaign, bonus is misaligned
tasks.fix: Change bonus to something more related to core value

tasks.description: Help them consume bonus AND engage with subscription
tasks.danger: If they only consume bonus, they'll cancel

tasks.task: Track bonus recipient retention vs. non-bonus
tasks.description: Monitor if bonus signups have different churn patterns
Get every product we've ever made FREE ($800 value) when you sign up for monthly shipments at $59/mo
Get all 40 past newsletters ($15,880 value) when you become a member for $399/mo after 30-day trial
Get our Short-Term Accelerator ($1000 value) FREE when you join VIP membership at $100/mo
Get lifetime access to premium templates ($500 value) when you subscribe to Pro at $29/mo

common_mistakes: Bonus value less than first payment (not compelling)
Bonus unrelated to core offer (attracts wrong people who churn)
Not enforcing TODAY-only deadline (loses urgency)
Forgetting to onboard on subscription value (just consume bonus and leave)
Not tracking bonus vs. non-bonus cohort retention
quick_wins: Bundle all past content/products as the bonus (high perceived value, zero marginal cost)
Add physical component to digital subscription (increases perceived value)
Make bonus consumption the first onboarding step (builds engagement)

commitment_discount.name: Free Duration with Commitment
commitment_discount.summary: Give X free months/services if they commit to Y months. Four approaches: Upfront, At the End, Spread Over Time, After First Payments. People think about monthly price, not total term.
commitment_discount.hormozi_principle: People think more about PRICE than TERM. They'll commit to 12 months if the monthly price is right, even if they'd never consciously choose a year contract.

tasks.description: This should be 1.33x to 3x the commitment price

tasks.task: Calculate commitment price with free months
tasks.description: Determine how many free months to include
Show monthly savings prominently
tasks.format: 'Pay $199/mo OR commit for 12 months and pay just $99/mo (save $1200!)'

tasks.description: Free trial period, then contract starts
tasks.best_for: When you need to enforce contracts (like cell phone carriers)

tasks.task: Option 2: AT THE END Free Time
tasks.description: Pay for X months, get Y free at the end
tasks.best_for: Reward loyal customers, reduce mid-contract churn
tasks.example: Pay for 9 months, get months 10-12 free

tasks.description: Discount applied every month across full term
tasks.example: Instead of $100/mo, pay $75/mo for all 12 months
tasks.psychology: Feels like ongoing savings every month

tasks.description: Pay normally for 1-2 months, then discount kicks in
Lead with the monthly savings, not the commitment
tasks.script: 'You can do $199/month with no commitment, or get the EXACT same thing for just $99/month...'
tasks.then: After they're interested in price: '...with our annual membership'

tasks.description: Calculate and display annual savings
tasks.format: 'Save $1,200 over the year' or 'Get 3 months FREE'

tasks.description: Side-by-side showing monthly vs. annual option
What happens if they try to cancel mid-commitment
options: Pay difference between discount and full rate for months used
tasks.principle: Make leaving cost more than staying

tasks.description: Don't surprise them—explain the commitment
tasks.script: 'This is a 12-month commitment. If life changes, you can cancel but would owe [X].'

common_mistakes: Standalone price too close to commitment price (not enough incentive)
Emphasizing the term instead of the price savings
No cancellation policy (they can just leave)
Cancellation policy too harsh (bad reviews, chargebacks)
Not testing which of the 4 application methods works best
quick_wins: Start with 2x price differential (70% should choose commitment)
Use 'Spread Over Time' method first (simplest to implement)
A/B test different commitment lengths (6mo vs 12mo vs 24mo)

waived_fee_continuity.name: Waived Fee with Commitment
waived_fee_continuity.summary: Waive your setup/onboarding fee (3-5x monthly rate) if they commit to 12+ months. If they cancel early, they pay the fee. Best for high-setup-cost businesses.

target_metrics.ltv: Fee waiver should pay off in additional months retained

waived_fee_continuity.hormozi_principle: Fee should be 3-5x your monthly rate. People will avoid paying a fee more than they'll seek a discount. Make leaving cost more than staying.

tasks.description: What does it actually cost to onboard a new customer?
Fee should be significant enough to deter early cancellation
tasks.principle: Larger fee = more choose commitment; Smaller fee = more upfront cash

tasks.description: At least 12 months to earn fee waiver
tasks.recommendation: 12 months minimum, consider 18-24 for higher-fee services

tasks.description: Justify the fee with real setup costs
tasks.script: 'Our onboarding involves [X, Y, Z] which costs us about $5,000 per client. That's why we charge a setup fee.'

tasks.task: Present Option A: Pay Fee + Month-to-Month
tasks.description: For those who want flexibility

tasks.task: Present Option B: Waive Fee + Commitment
tasks.description: For those who want to save
tasks.format: 'Or, commit to 12 months and we'll waive the $5,000 fee entirely. You just pay $1,000/month.'

tasks.description: Present both options and ask which they prefer

tasks.task: Define fee collection on early cancel
tasks.description: If they break commitment, they pay the waived fee
tasks.script: 'If you need to cancel before 12 months, the $5,000 setup fee becomes due.'
tasks.clear: Explain this upfront, get signed agreement

tasks.description: Some businesses prorate based on time served
tasks.example: Cancel at month 6 = Pay $2,500 (half the fee)

tasks.description: Document the terms legally
People hate losing money more than they like saving it
tasks.application: The fee they'd have to PAY if they cancel feels worse than the fee they SAVED

tasks.description: At any point, the cost to cancel should exceed cost to continue
tasks.example: At month 8 with 4 months left at $1,000 = $4,000 to stay. Cancel fee = $5,000. Staying is cheaper.

common_mistakes: Fee too small (not enough deterrent)
Fee too large (feels unreasonable, causes disputes)
Not explaining fee rationale (feels like a trap)
Not getting signed agreement (can't enforce)
Commitment too short (12 months minimum)
quick_wins: Start with 3x monthly as fee (test higher later)
Use clear contract language reviewed by legal
Train team to present BOTH options equally (let customer choose)

downsell_to_continuity.name: Big Head, Long Tail (Downsell Upsell)
downsell_to_continuity.summary: Sell a high upfront payment PLUS a small monthly fee. Get more cash upfront by selling shorter duration with added value for less. People focus on monthly price over term.
downsell_to_continuity.hormozi_principle: People think about MONTHLY CASH FLOW more than DURATION. The power of commitments and contracts dramatically increases LTV. Price divided by churn rate equals lifetime revenue.

tasks.description: Upfront payment for initial value/training
tasks.pricing: Should cover your acquisition and initial delivery costs

tasks.description: Ongoing monthly value delivery
tasks.pricing: Lower than what they'd pay for standalone monthly

tasks.task: Calculate the math vs. one-time sale
tasks.description: Compare total value over 12-20 months
tasks.example: One-time: $1,000. Big Head + Tail: $500 + $50/mo × 20 months = $1,500. LTV increased 50%.

tasks.task: Set monthly lower than psychological threshold
tasks.description: Monthly should feel 'almost nothing'
tasks.principle: People accept small ongoing payments more than large one-time

tasks.description: Compare to buying separately
tasks.example: 'Training: $500 + Monthly coaching: $100/mo = $1,700/year. OR: Join now and get both for $500 + just $50/mo = $1,100/year'

tasks.task: Use churn rate to project LTV
tasks.description: Price / Churn Rate = Lifetime Revenue
Start from their positive experience
Get buy-in before presenting
tasks.script: 'Mind if I tell you about a way to save a little and get more?'

tasks.description: Frame as partnership
tasks.script: 'Given you've enjoyed [current offer], we want you here long-term. Here's what we're gonna do...'

tasks.description: More value for less monthly
tasks.script: 'If you're in this with us for the long term, we want to reward you with MORE stuff for LESS. Sound good?'

tasks.description: Justify continuity with ongoing value delivery
tasks.principle: They should get more in the long tail, not just pay for less

tasks.description: The 'big head' gives immediate results
The 'long tail' keeps them engaged

common_mistakes: Monthly fee too high (feels like another large purchase)
No real value in the ongoing (just 'access')
Not tracking months retained (don't know if it's working)
Big head too small (doesn't cover acquisition costs)
Not adding ongoing value (just extracting money)
quick_wins: Start with existing product, add monthly community/coaching
Set monthly at 10% of one-time price (feels small)
Create one new piece of content/value per month minimum

auto_replenishment.name: Auto-Replenishment Subscription
auto_replenishment.summary: Automatically ship consumable physical products on a recurring schedule. Customers never run out, you get predictable revenue. Best for products with natural consumption cycles.
auto_replenishment.hormozi_principle: For consumable products, the question isn't IF they'll buy again, but WHERE. Make it easier to stay subscribed than to shop around.

tasks.description: Product must be used up and need replacement
How often do customers typically need to reorder?
tasks.method: Survey existing customers or track reorder patterns

tasks.description: Can you offer discount and still profit?
tasks.formula: (Subscription Price - COGS - Shipping) × Avg Months Retained = Profit per Subscriber

tasks.description: Same product delivered on schedule
Different/curated products each delivery
Ongoing access plus new releases
Select based on product type and customer preference
Never run out, automatic delivery
tasks.copy: 'Never worry about running out. We'll deliver automatically.'

tasks.description: Discount vs. one-time purchase
Subscriber-only benefits
Reduce commitment anxiety
tasks.copy: 'Skip, pause, or cancel anytime. No questions asked.'

tasks.description: Platform for managing recurring orders
Let customers skip a delivery instead of canceling
Let customers change frequency, quantity, products
Reduce shipping costs for recurring orders
Track if customers are accumulating product (sign they'll cancel)
Occasional free gifts or upgrades for subscribers
Re-engage cancelled subscribers
tasks.offer: Special discount or bonus to return

common_mistakes: Shipping costs eat into profit (optimize logistics)
No skip option (forces cancellation instead of pause)
Discount too deep (not profitable)
Discount too small (not compelling)
Not tracking product accumulation (surprise cancellations)
quick_wins: Offer Subscribe & Save on product pages (15% off)
Implement skip functionality before anything else

pure_subscription.name: Pure Monthly Subscription/Membership
pure_subscription.summary: Simple recurring monthly or annual subscription for access to content, software, community, or services. The cleanest continuity model when you can deliver ongoing value.

target_metrics.churn_rate: Under 5% for SaaS, under 10% for content/coaching
target_metrics.cac_recovery: Months to recover Customer Acquisition Cost

pure_subscription.hormozi_principle: The best businesses have recurring revenue at their core. LTGP (Lifetime Gross Profit) is what matters: Gross Margin × Lifetime Value. Optimize for both.

tasks.description: What do subscribers get each month?
tasks.principle: Must be valuable enough that they'd miss it if gone

tasks.description: Plan what you'll deliver each month
tasks.minimum: At least one new valuable thing per month

tasks.description: What outcome does the subscription help them achieve?
Based on value delivered and market positioning
15-20% discount for annual commitment
tasks.bonus: Bill every 4 weeks instead of monthly = 8.3% more annual revenue

tasks.description: Multiple levels for different needs/budgets
7-30 days to demonstrate value
tasks.decision: Trial length based on time needed to show value

tasks.description: Key actions new subscribers must take
Emails guiding them through first week
Track engagement to identify at-risk subscribers
Offer alternatives before they leave
tasks.script: 'Before you cancel, let me show you some options...'

tasks.description: Understand why and offer to solve
tasks.question: 'What would have to change for you to stay?'
tasks.outcome: Either solve it or learn for future

tasks.description: Re-engage cancelled members
tasks.offer: Special return offer or show what they've missed

tasks.description: Reach out when engagement drops
tasks.trigger: No login in X days, or usage below threshold
tasks.action: Personal email or call to check in

tasks.description: Total monthly subscription revenue
% of subscribers who cancel each month
Lifetime Gross Profit = Gross Margin × LTV
tasks.formula: LTV = Monthly Price / Churn Rate. LTGP = LTV × Gross Margin %

tasks.description: Are existing customers expanding or contracting?
How many months to recover acquisition cost?

common_mistakes: No new value each month (people feel stuck)
Not monitoring engagement (surprise churn)
Making cancellation too easy (no save attempts)
Making cancellation too hard (bad reviews, chargebacks)
Not tracking unit economics (unprofitable growth)
quick_wins: Add pause option to cancellation flow (keeps billing relationship)
Implement 'what you'll miss' email after cancellation
Create subscriber-only benefit that's visible (FOMO for non-subscribers)
